date: 17 October 2026; Lechuza and Benteveo recast on October 20-21, 2026
intro_html:
Read this first. I could not listen to any of this. Every judgement below comes from measurements, and they are crude. Please listen before anything ships, starting with Benteveo.

How the voices were made. Each neighbour's voice was designed from a written Spanish description with Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign. Each description named the man, his age and timbre, and the old Buenos Aires sound: ll/y as a buzzing "zh" [ʒ], aspirated s, the Italian rise and fall, and vos. Every candidate read the same short test: ll/y words, vos, c/z words, then an urgent shout. 56 candidates in all: 12 for Hornero, 12 for Lechuza, 24 for Benteveo and 8 for Biguá. Then all 64 lines, Spanish and English, were cloned three times each from the chosen design take with Qwen3-TTS Base. The best take was picked by what Whisper heard, then by how closely it matches the design voice (ECAPA), then by length and pitch. Benteveo was moved down two semitones in the game until October 20; since the recast nobody is shifted. The English lines are cloned from the Spanish voice, so they carry its accent. No recording of anyone was used.

The accent check. For every ll/y word in a test take, I measured whether the consonant hisses (energy at 3–8 kHz, compared with an s in the same take). A [ʒ] or [ʃ] hisses; the [ʝ]/[j] of Spain, Mexico and most other Spanish does not. Where there was hiss, I checked whether voicing ran under it (energy below 400 Hz). The 1958 [ʒ] is voiced; today's porteño [ʃ] is not. To see whether the check means anything, the same model read the same text in a Madrid voice and a Mexico City voice (both below). Those four takes hissed on 1 ll/y word in 5 at most. The chosen porteños hissed on 2–4 of 4–5. In the final Spanish game lines, all 9 ll/y sounds hiss above the Madrid/Mexico level: 4 voiced, 5 voiceless.

What that means, honestly. The model clearly knows the Rioplatense hiss: these voices have it and the Madrid and Mexico voices don't. But much of it is the modern voiceless "sh" of today's Buenos Aires, not the voiced "zh" of 1958, even though every description asked for the buzz. Nothing here measures the Italian melody beyond the pitch range, or the aspirated s. Whisper's language ID cannot tell Rioplatense from any other Spanish. My expectation is that a porteño will hear voices with a Rioplatense flavour on a fairly neutral synthetic base: a few telling sounds, not a 1958 Boca accent. That is the limit of a designed synthetic voice without a reference recording. For the English, Whisper is less sure these four are speaking English (mean P(English) 0.71–0.83) than it is for Wren, Rook, Merle and Rype (0.86–0.98). Its mishearings are the classic Spanish-speaker ones: "live" heard as "leave", "fuse" as "foose", "done" as "don't", "yeta" as "dieta". So the accent comes through. Whether it reads as Argentine or as Spanish-speaking in general can't be measured.

Pitch. These are medians of the calm lines in the game. Biguá is about 88 Hz, the bass. Hornero is about 113 Hz. Lechuza, recast on October 20 as a man of about seventy, is about 113 Hz (he was about 165, a thin older voice). Benteveo, recast the same day as a boy of twelve or thirteen whose voice has not broken, is about 370 Hz in his calm lines, which are nearly all shouted, and about 550 in his alarms (he was about 205 after the shift). The urgent lines run 6–9 semitones higher. For comparison, Rook is about 90–100 Hz, Wren about 110 (about 80 Hz in his shifted English) and Rype about 140. Biguá sits at Rook's pitch and Hornero near Wren's. They never share an operation.

The recast of October 20-21 (Lechuza, Benteveo). Same method, on this Mac, in float32 (bfloat16 has no fast CPU kernels here). Lechuza's description became an old man's: seventy, cracked and rasping, slow, breathy, ironic. Benteveo's became a boy's of twelve or thirteen, before the voice breaks (his first description, a sixteen-year-old's, had been pushed towards a tenor and then shifted down). Twenty candidates each (A, B, Z, and C and D, which say the age plainly). The model took "grave" hard for Lechuza: nine candidates came out at 73-92 Hz; the five between 95 and 125 Hz were judged by the words, the ll/y hiss, the duration (slow is right) and a crude harmonic-to-noise figure (rough is right). For Benteveo the model now makes children without being asked twice: fourteen of twenty above 300 Hz. His clones run 60-70 Hz above his design take: the Base model shouts his exclamation marks.

calibration.M2: Calibration, never cast: the same model and text, described as a man from Madrid. No hiss on any ll/y word.
calibration.X1: Calibration, never cast: described as a man from Mexico City. Hiss on 1 of 5 ll/y words.

hornero.verdict: Recommended: Z2. Of Hornero's 12 candidates it came closest to the 1958 buzz: "llueve", "yo" and "ayer" all hiss with voicing under them ("calle" and "ya" came out as a plain [j]). Whisper heard every word, Spanish 97%. Its urgent half rises 7 semitones, so his spotted and hurt lines have some alarm. At about 113 Hz in the game he sits between Biguá and Lechuza. Honest guess: a calm, dry middle-aged porteño with a few clear "zh"s, not a heavy accent.

candidates.Z2: 118 Hz; Whisper es 97%, all words right; ll/y: 3 of 5 hiss, all 3 voiced (zh); melody range 10 st.
candidates.A1: Runner-up. 94 Hz, the warmest and deepest baritone of the twelve; words all right; ll/y 2 of 5 (one voiced). Its urgent half barely rises (+2 st), and it would sit on top of Biguá's pitch.
candidates.Z3: Runner-up. 114 Hz, the most sing-song of Hornero's candidates (21 st range); ll/y 2 of 5, both voiceless (the modern 'sh'). The one to try if Z2 sounds too plain.

lechuza.verdict: Recast October 20: C2 (the long "anciano" description with the buzz). 113 Hz in the design and in the game, every word heard right, Spanish 96%, 2 of 4 ll/y hiss (1 voiced), the slowest read of the five in the 95-125 Hz band (15.0 s) and one of the roughest by the harmonic-to-noise figure. Alarms about 150-165 Hz. I could not listen: whether he sounds seventy, or merely low and hoarse, only an ear can say. The previous voice, A1 (166 Hz), was 55 by description.

candidates.C2: 113 Hz; Whisper es 96%, all words right; ll/y: 2 of 4 hiss (1 voiced); 15.0 s, rough (chosen).
candidates.D3: Runner-up. 109 Hz, the roughest in the band, lively melody (16 st), but "Mirabos, vive" and a dropped syllable.
candidates.Z3: Runner-up. 104 Hz, every word right, 2 of 4 ll/y hiss; the smoothest voice of the twenty: a healthy baritone rather than an old man.
candidates.A3: Not kept: 92 Hz, just under the band, both hissing ll/y voiced (the 1958 buzz), 15.1 s. The one to try if 113 Hz is not deep enough.

benteveo.verdict: Recast October 20: C1 (the long "nene" description with the buzz). A child's voice by every figure: 309 Hz in the calm part of the design, shouts to about 560; every word heard right, Spanish 97%, 4 of 5 ll/y hiss (2 voiced), the liveliest melody of his twenty (16 st). Cloned, his lines come out higher than the design: about 370 Hz in the calm ones (nearly all are exclamations) and about 550 in the alarms. No shift in the game any more. Listen for whether he sounds twelve or younger; if too high, A1 (246 Hz, the fastest read) is the lowest candidate that is still a child, with the risk of a young woman's register.

candidates.C1: 309 Hz calm, 383 overall; Whisper es 97%, all words right; ll/y 4 of 5 hiss (2 voiced); melody 16 st (chosen).
candidates.C2: Runner-up. 320 Hz; all words right; all 5 ll/y hiss, none voiced (today's 'sh').
candidates.Z4: Runner-up. 276 Hz; 4 of 5 ll/y hiss (1 voiced); the shout heard as "Cara, cara".
candidates.A1: Not kept: 246 Hz, the lowest in the 240-320 band and the fastest read (8.9 s), all words right; its loud frames sit near 195 Hz.

bigua.verdict: Recommended: A4. The deepest voice of all 56 (89 Hz), and the most consistent hiss: all 4 ll/y words. But all 4 are voiceless, so this is today's porteño 'sh', not the 1958 'zh'. Of the four, Biguá is the most clearly Buenos Aires and the least 1958. Whisper heard every word, Spanish 97%. His shout rises 6.5 semitones and 7 dB. If the period buzz matters more than depth, A1 hisses on all 4 with 2 voiced, but it sits on Hornero's pitch.

candidates.A4: 89 Hz, the bass; Whisper es 97%, all words right; ll/y: 4 of 4 hiss, all voiceless ('sh').
candidates.A1: Runner-up. 105–110 Hz; ll/y 4 of 4 hiss, 2 voiced (orilla, ya): more 1958, but too close to Hornero.
candidates.A2: Runner-up. 110 Hz; ll/y 3 of 4 (1 voiced); clean and calm.
